newsitem.title: HONG KONG: No change for Taiwan business in HK - Tung adviser.
newsitem.headline: No change for Taiwan business in HK - Tung adviser.

text.p: Taiwan businesses in Hong Kong will be treated the same as companies from anywhere else after the territory is handed back to Beijing, an aide to Hong Kong's future leader was quoted on Monday as saying.

Paul Yip Kwok-wah, a special adviser to Hong Kong's chief executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa, told The South China Morning Post that all businesses, whether from Hong Kong, the United States, South Korea, Taiwan or elsewhere would be treated the same.
"Hong Kong will implement 'one country, two systems' and will be different from the mainland," said Yip.
"One country, two systems" is the formula under which Hong Kong will retain a large degree of autonomy after its handover to China at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday.
Chinese Nationalists fled to Taiwan after a 1949 civil war defeat at the hands of the Communists led to the establishment of the People's Republic of China.
Since then Taiwan has used Hong Kong as a bridgehead for investment and travel into China, with which it does not have direct relations.

The newspaper also quoted Koo Chen-fu, chairman of Taiwan's non-official Straits Exchange Foundation, as saying continuation of the existing economic and trade system was important after the handover.
Koo would attend the swearing in of Tung as chief executive, it said.
